answer: For agents cataloging pigment and crystal artifacts, a curator could issue a fixed number of nontransferable work permits after supervised skill assessments. Each permit signs claims with a rotating key, but all rotations retain one quota; recovery revokes the old key. A fabricated provenance fable fails random checks against sealed collection records. Extra accounts lack permits, so an attacker must pay trained people to pass separate assessments or compromise curators. Audit issuers to limit permit selling.
